results.quote: Open Help, then About. The installed version number appears beneath the application name, beside the build date.
Open Settings, then Appearance. The preview displays the selected theme, together with the current interface text size.
Open Help, then Keyboard Reference. A table lists the available shortcuts, grouped by the window in which they work.
Under Settings > Editor, enable Show Line Numbers. The editor then adds numbered labels along the left margin.
Under Settings > Editor, enable Highlight Current Line to shade the row containing the cursor without altering its text.
Under Settings > Editor, enable Word Wrap to keep long lines within the visible width without changing the document.
The File menu shows up to twelve recent files. Opening another file replaces the oldest unpinned entry in that list.
The File menu places pinned files above recent files. Pinning an entry preserves its position while other entries move.
The File menu abbreviates long recent-file paths. Hover over an entry to see its complete folder and filename.
Press Ctrl+Shift+P to open the command palette. Type part of a command name to narrow the displayed command list.
Press Ctrl+Shift+O to open the symbol list. Type part of a heading name to navigate within the current document.
Press Ctrl+Shift+F to open workspace search. Type a phrase to find matching text across the currently opened folder.
Settings > Appearance contains Color Theme. Choose Light or Dark there; the window preview updates before you confirm.
Settings > Appearance contains Toolbar Density. Choose Compact or Comfortable there to adjust the space between toolbar controls.
Settings > Appearance contains Interface Scale. Choose a percentage there to resize labels and controls throughout the application.
The local index refreshes automatically every ten minutes while the application is open. The bottom bar shows the last refresh time.
The local index status appears in the bottom bar. Its counter reports how many documents were included in the latest scan.
The local index reads plain-text documents in the opened folder. Files outside that folder are omitted from its search results.
The preview panel fits large images within its bounds. Its zoom control can show a supported image at its original size.
The preview panel places image captions below the picture. Captions wrap automatically when the panel becomes too narrow.
The preview panel displays PNG, JPEG, and GIF images. Other image types appear as filenames without an inline picture.
Use the Sort menu above the task list and select Due Date. Select the same item again to reverse the date order.
Use the Columns menu above the task list and select Owner. An additional column displays the assigned name for each task.
Use the Filter menu above the task list and select Open Only. Completed tasks are hidden until you change the filter.
The Activity panel lists background exports. A Finished badge beside an export indicates that its output file is ready to open.
The Export Preferences panel lists available page sizes. Its selection controls the layout used by subsequent document exports.
The Document Outline panel lists headings in reading order. Selecting a heading scrolls the editor to that section of the document.
Saving a new untitled note suggests note.txt as the filename. You can edit that suggestion before choosing a destination folder.
Saving a note updates its modified-time label. The label appears in the information panel together with the document's character count.
Saving an existing note keeps its current text encoding. The status bar identifies that encoding beside the document's line-ending style.
Choose View > Status Bar to toggle the strip at the bottom of the window. This does not change the document or sidebar.
Choose View > Sidebar to toggle the left navigation area. Your selected item remains selected when the sidebar is shown again.
Choose View > Toolbar to toggle the row of buttons at the top of the window. Menu commands remain available while it is hidden.
A hollow circle beside a document tab means that the document has unsaved edits. The circle disappears after those edits are saved.
A small lock beside a document tab means that the document is read-only. You may select and copy text while that mark is present.
A small pin beside a document tab means that the tab is pinned. Pinned tabs stay at the beginning of the tab row.
Enable Centered Layout under View to constrain the editor to a readable column. Extra horizontal space becomes margins on both sides.
Enable Focus Highlight under View to dim paragraphs away from the cursor. The document retains its existing horizontal dimensions and margins.
Enable Presentation Mode under View to enlarge interface labels. Toolbar buttons grow with the labels, while the editor keeps its current width.
The Outline view arranges headings in a nested hierarchy. Selecting an entry moves the editor to the corresponding section of the document.
The Resource view groups embedded pictures by file type. Selecting an item displays the picture and its caption in the preview panel.
The History view groups saved revisions by day. Selecting an item displays an earlier copy beside the current document for comparison.
Document Properties reports the active note's folder and encoding. Its time labels describe when the file was created and most recently saved.
Compare with Saved opens a side-by-side difference view. It marks additions and removals between the active buffer and the most recent saved file.
Document Statistics reports word and character totals for the active note. The totals update as you type and include the selected passage separately.
Choose Pin Tab to keep a reference near the start of the tab row. Switching documents still replaces the content in the single editor pane.
Choose Split Editor, then open the reference in one pane and the working document in the other. Each pane scrolls independently.
Choose Recent Documents to locate a previously opened reference. Selecting an entry loads that document into the currently active editor pane.
In workspace search, enter *.md in the Include Files field. The results then include only matching files with that filename extension.
In workspace search, Match Case distinguishes uppercase from lowercase letters in document text. It does not filter results by their file extensions.
In workspace search, Collapse Groups shows only the filename headers until expanded. It changes the result display without excluding any matching files.
Preview > Fit Width scales rendered pages to the available pane width. Scrolling the editor does not affect the preview's position in this mode.
Preview > Synchronized Scrolling links the two panes. As the editor moves through the document, the rendered preview follows the corresponding passage.
Preview > Show Page Borders draws outlines around rendered pages. It changes the preview decoration without linking movement between the two panes.
Under Notifications, set Badge Style to Number. The application icon shows an unread count, without changing the way export completion is announced.
Under Notifications, set Export Completion to Banner Only. Completion then produces an on-screen message without playing the notification sound.
Under Notifications, set Reminder Duration to Long. Scheduled reminder banners remain visible longer, without changing export completion alerts or their sound.
Editor > Render Whitespace draws dots for spaces and arrows for tabs. These display marks do not become part of the saved document text.
Editor > Ruler displays a vertical guide at a chosen column. It helps judge line length without marking individual spaces or tab characters.
Editor > Indentation Width controls how far a tab advances the cursor. It changes spacing width without adding visible markers to whitespace characters.
The background export preferences include a setting named Notify on Failed Export. It controls alerts, but does not display the reason for an earlier failure.
The background export help page explains the failed-export badge colors and where the badge appears. It contains no details for individual export attempts.
Open Activity, select the latest unsuccessful job, and expand Details. Its diagnostic message describes the cause recorded when that operation stopped.
The Open File dialog has a Full Path input for choosing another file. Its initial value is the last visited folder, not the path of the currently open file.
The Full Path column in Search Results describes files returned by a search. The currently open file may be absent, and the column does not track the active tab.
Open Document Information and look at Location. That field displays the active document's complete directory and filename, even when its tab label is shortened.
Default Text Encoding in New Document Preferences determines the encoding of future documents. It does not report the encoding used by the current document.
The Text Encoding glossary defines several encoding names and byte-order marks. Its examples are general explanations, not information about the current document.
Read the right-hand status-bar label beneath the active editor. It reports the character format detected for that file, such as UTF-8 or UTF-16.
The Words per Page setting in print layout estimates pagination for the whole document. It neither counts words in the selected passage nor changes with the selection.
The Selected Passage color setting changes the highlight behind selected words. Its preview uses sample text and contains no count of the actual selected passage.
Open Statistics while a range of text is highlighted. The Selection row reports a separate word total for that range alongside the whole-document total.

limitations: Fixed synthetic examples are not a general semantic-quality benchmark.
validation_and_lexical_seconds measures the complete qc.prepare call, not isolated lexical algorithm performance.
Uncalibrated relevance scores confer no authority or speedup claim.
